- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- mw-cp: Mike Wright's Checkpoint Process — pre-commit checks, doc updates, detailed commit, and push
- claude-mem:do: Execute a plan using subagents for implementation
- claude-mem:make-plan: Create an implementation plan with documentation discovery
- claude-mem:mem-search: Search claude-mem's persistent cross-session memory database. Use when user asks "did we already solve this?", "how did we do X last time?", or needs work from previous sessions.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request

I want to focus my ML PL on more ML data types as first class language features and separate out tools into optional libraries.  I'm thinking of concepts like logit, layer, attention head, and operations like back-propogate, softmax, sinkhorn normalization, etc.  what would be a good candidate list for such building blocks in a programming language designed to manipulate and visualize them, show shape, graphs, animate transforms, etc.

I’ll treat this as a language-design inventory problem: separate core semantic data types from optional algorithm/tool libraries, while keeping visualization, shape tracking, and transform animation in mind.

Thought for a few seconds
You want the ML PL core to make ML-native values visible, inspectable, composable, and type/shape-aware, while moving larger workflows and integrations into libraries. A good split is:

1. Core first-class data types
Category	Candidate first-class types	Why they belong in the language core
Numeric/scalar	Scalar, Probability, LogProbability, Logit, Loss, Gradient	These carry meaning beyond “float.” A Logit should not be silently treated as a probability.
Shape-aware arrays	Tensor, Vector, Matrix, Axis, Shape, Batch, Sequence, Channel	Shape and axis meaning are central to ML debugging and visualization.
Distributions	Distribution, Categorical, Gaussian, Mixture, EmbeddingDistribution	Useful for sampling, uncertainty, generative models, and visual explanations.
Neural structure	Layer, Module, Parameter, ParameterSet, Activation, Residual, Normalization	Lets models be inspected as structured objects, not opaque functions.
Attention	Token, Embedding, Query, Key, Value, AttentionHead, AttentionMap, AttentionBlock	Excellent candidates because they have visualizable intermediate states.
Graph/autodiff	ComputationGraph, Node, Edge, Tape, ForwardPass, BackwardPass, Jacobian, Hessian	Enables animation of forward/backward flow and dependency tracing.
Training state	OptimizerState, LearningRate, Momentum, BatchStats, Checkpoint, Epoch, Step	Useful, but maybe “core-adjacent” rather than minimal core.
Data/model IO	Dataset, Sample, Label, Feature, BatchStream, Transform	First-class if your language is also for teaching/dataflow visualization.
2. Core operations worth making language-visible
Operation family	Candidate operations
Tensor ops	reshape, permute, slice, broadcast, contract, matmul, einsum, concat, split
Probability/logit ops	softmax, log_softmax, sigmoid, temperature_scale, argmax, top_k, sample
Normalization	normalize, layer_norm, batch_norm, rms_norm, sinkhorn_normalize
Attention	project_qkv, score_attention, mask_attention, apply_attention, multi_head_attention
Autodiff	forward, backward, backpropagate, gradient, stop_gradient, detach, checkpoint_gradient
Losses	cross_entropy, mse, kl_divergence, contrastive_loss, triplet_loss
Optimizers	step, zero_grad, clip_grad, sgd, adam, adamw
Visualization hooks	trace, inspect_shape, show_graph, animate, compare, explain_transform
3. Strong candidates for language primitives
These feel like the best “first-class” building blocks:

Tensor
Shape
Axis
Logit
Probability
Distribution
Parameter
Gradient
Layer
Activation
AttentionHead
AttentionMap
ComputationGraph
ForwardPass
BackwardPass
Loss
OptimizerState
Dataset
Transform
The reason: each has semantic meaning, visual structure, and common misuse cases that a language can prevent.

4. Things better as optional libraries
These are important, but probably not core syntax/types at first:

CNN layers
Transformer variants
Diffusion schedulers
RL environments
Fine-tuning frameworks
Model loaders
ONNX / GGUF / safetensors support
CUDA / MLX / WebGPU backends
Dataset downloaders
Tokenizer implementations
Experiment tracking
The language core should know what an AttentionHead is; a library can provide LlamaAttention, ViTBlock, or StableDiffusionUNet.

5. A useful organizing principle
Design the language around observable transforms:

value_before
  -> operation
  -> value_after
  -> shape change
  -> graph change
  -> visual animation
  -> gradient consequence
So a statement like:

p : Probability[Batch, Token] =
    softmax(logits : Logit[Batch, Token], axis: Token)
could automatically expose:

input shape:  [Batch, Token]
output shape: [Batch, Token]
axis meaning: Token
domain:       Logit -> Probability
visual:       bars/surface/heatmap
gradient:     differentiable
6. My recommended MVP core
For a first useful prototype:

Tensor
Shape
Axis
Logit
Probability
Layer
Parameter
Gradient
ComputationGraph
AttentionHead
AttentionMap
Loss
Dataset
Transform
And implement these operations first:

reshape
matmul
softmax
log_softmax
cross_entropy
forward
backward
gradient
layer_norm
attention
sinkhorn_normalize
trace
animate
show_shape
show_graph
That gives you enough to demonstrate:

logits -> softmax -> loss -> backprop -> gradient update
and:

tokens -> embeddings -> Q/K/V -> attention map -> attended values
Those two pipelines would make the language feel genuinely ML-native rather than just “Python with tensor syntax.”

1	# Saga
2	
3	## Saga -1: Repo scaffolding (COMPLETE)
4	Repo compartmentalization scaffolding.
5	
6	## Saga 0: Foundation (COMPLETE)
7	Foundation and contracts.
8	
9	## Saga 1: Dense tensor substrate v1 (COMPLETE)
10	Shape, DenseArray, reshape, transpose, indexing.
11	
12	## Saga 2: Parser and evaluator foundation (COMPLETE)
13	Lexer, AST, parser with precedence, AST-walking evaluator.
14	
15	## Saga 3: CLI and REPL v1 (COMPLETE)
16	Working REPL with all v1 syntax, built-in functions, tracing.
17	
18	## Saga 4: Structured trace v1 (COMPLETE)
19	TraceEvent/Trace types, evaluator instrumentation, JSON export.
20	
21	## Saga 5: Visual web viewer v1 (DEFERRED)
22	Deferred to post-MVP. MVP uses CLI + JSON trace export.
23	
24	## MVP
25	Sagas 0 through 4 complete. MVP ships with REPL + trace export.
26	
27	## Saga 6: ML foundations (COMPLETE)
28	Sigmoid, tanh_fn, pow, comparison operators, axis reductions, mean,
29	array constructors (zeros, ones, fill), and the first end-to-end
30	logistic regression demo. Delivered v0.2.
31	
32	## Saga 7: SVG visualization v1 (COMPLETE)
33	`mlpl-viz` crate, `svg(data, type[, aux])` built-in, diagram types
34	(scatter, line, bar, heatmap, decision_boundary), `grid()` helper,
35	high-level analysis helpers (hist, scatter_labeled, loss_curve,
36	confusion_matrix, boundary_2d), browser REPL inline SVG rendering,
37	and download button. Delivered v0.3.
38	
39	## Saga 11: Model DSL (COMPLETE)
40	Composition primitives for neural-net models: a new `Value::Model`
41	runtime value, atomic `linear(in, out, seed)` layers,
42	parameter-free activation layers (`tanh_layer`, `relu_layer`,
43	`softmax_layer`), sequential `chain(...)` composition,
44	`residual(block)` skip connections, `rms_norm(dim)` normalization,
45	and `attention(d_model, heads, seed)` multi-head self-attention
46	(tape-lowered for `heads=1`, forward-only for `heads>1`). A
47	`params(model)` walker returns the flat parameter list, and
48	optimizers now accept a model identifier directly so
49	`adam(loss, mdl, lr, b1, b2, eps)` trains every weight the model
50	owns through differentiable `apply(mdl, X)`. The v0.6 `moons_mlp`
51	and `tiny_mlp` demos were rewritten as one-line `chain(...)`
52	expressions, and a new `transformer_block.mlpl` demo stacks
53	`residual(chain(rms_norm, attention))` and `residual(chain(
54	rms_norm, linear, relu_layer, linear))` twice to train a tiny
55	2-layer transformer block end-to-end (loss 143.87 -> 1.02 over
56	100 Adam steps, strictly monotonic). New REPL introspection
57	commands -- `:vars`, `:models`, `:fns`, `:wsid`, `:describe` --
58	ship in both `mlpl-repl` and `mlpl-web`, and a new "Model
59	Composition" tutorial lesson walks from a single `linear` through
60	a chain MLP to Adam inside `train { }` on the moons dataset.
61	Delivered v0.7. See `docs/milestone-modeldsl.md`.
62	
63	## Saga 10: Optimizers + training loop (COMPLETE)
64	Built proper training infrastructure on top of Saga 9 autograd.
65	New built-ins: `momentum_sgd(loss, params, lr, beta)` and
66	`adam(loss, params, lr, b1, b2, eps)` with per-parameter state
67	held in an `OptimizerState` map on the evaluation environment;
68	`cosine_schedule(step, total, lr_min, lr_max)` and
69	`linear_warmup(step, warmup, lr)` pure scalar schedules; and
70	two non-linear synthetic datasets `moons(seed, n, noise)` and
71	`circles(seed, n, noise)` returning `[N, 3]` `[x, y, label]`
72	matrices in the same layout as `blobs`. New `train N { body }`
73	language construct binds the iteration index to `step` inside
74	the body and captures each iteration's final value into a
75	`last_losses` 1-D array, replacing the manual
76	`repeat { grad; manual update; record loss }` recipe. Two new
77	demos -- `demos/moons_mlp.mlpl` and `demos/circles_mlp.mlpl` --
78	train a tanh MLP with `adam` inside `train { }` and render the
79	decision boundary with `boundary_2d`. New "Optimizers and
80	Schedules" tutorial lesson added to the web REPL. Delivered v0.6.
81	
82	## Saga 9: Autograd v1 (COMPLETE)
83	Reverse-mode autograd as a language primitive. New `mlpl-autograd`
84	crate provides a tape-based `Tensor` with backward over add, sub,
85	mul, div, neg, exp, log, relu, tanh, sigmoid, softmax, sum, mean,
86	transpose, reshape, and matmul, all gradcheck-verified against
87	finite differences. Parser surface adds `param[shape]` and
88	`tensor[shape]` constructors, and a new `grad(expr, wrt)` built-in
89	lifts array expressions onto the tape and returns the gradient
90	with respect to a tracked parameter. The v0.4 `tiny_mlp` and
91	`softmax_classifier` demos were ported to use `param + grad`
92	instead of hand-written backprop, and a new "Automatic
93	Differentiation" tutorial lesson walks from a scalar minimization
94	to a one-layer linear regression. Delivered v0.5.
95	
96	## Saga 8: ML demos (COMPLETE)
97	Synthetic data primitives (random, randn, argmax, blobs) and
98	higher-level ML built-ins (softmax, one_hot), plus six demos wired
99	into the browser REPL: k-means clustering, PCA via power iteration,
100	a linear softmax classifier, a tiny MLP on XOR-style data, and a
101	scaled dot-product attention pattern. Tutorial lessons added for
102	each. Delivered v0.4.
103	
104	## Saga 11.5: Named Axes and shape introspection (COMPLETE)
105	Axis-labeled shapes threaded through `Value::Array` via a new
106	`LabeledShape` type on `mlpl-core`. `label(x, [...])` and `relabel(x,
107	[...])` primitives, annotation syntax on assignment (`x : [batch,
108	time, dim] = ...`), and `reshape_labeled(x, dims, labels)` as the
109	opt-in re-labeling path. Label propagation through elementwise
110	ops (with one-None-one-Some accepted and mismatches rejected),
111	matmul (contraction axis validated, outer dims passed through),
112	reduce/argmax (reduced axis's label dropped), and `map()`
113	(preserves labels through every math builtin). `reduce_add`,
114	`reduce_mul`, `argmax`, and `softmax` accept an axis name string
115	in place of an integer. Structured `EvalError::ShapeMismatch
116	{ op, expected: LabeledShape, actual: LabeledShape }` at the
117	evaluator boundary, with Display rendering as `op: expected
118	[seq=N, d=M], got [time=N, d=M]`. Label-aware `:vars` and
119	`:describe` (using `LabeledShape` Display), and trace JSON that
120	round-trips axis labels for labeled arrays and omits the key
121	entirely for unlabeled ones. New "Named Axes" tutorial lesson in
122	the web REPL; "Model Composition" lesson now annotates X as
123	`[batch, feat]` so labels flow through `apply(mdl, X)`. Delivered
124	v0.7.5. See `docs/milestone-named-axes.md`.
125	
126	## Saga: Compile-to-Rust (COMPLETE)
127	Lowers MLPL source to Rust `TokenStream` shared by three targets:
128	the `mlpl!` proc macro (compile-time embed inside Rust apps), the
129	`mlpl build foo.mlpl -o bin` subcommand (native-binary and
130	cross-compile via cargo+rustc, verified for native and
131	wasm32-unknown-unknown), and a leaner future WASM path that
132	reuses the same pipeline. New crates: `mlpl-rt` (runtime target;
133	typed primitive wrappers around `DenseArray`/`LabeledShape`),
134	`mlpl-lower-rs` (AST -> `TokenStream` with path-configurable
135	runtime prefix and static matmul contraction checks when both
136	operands' labels are known at lower time), `mlpl-macro`
137	(proc-macro wrapper), `mlpl` (user-facing facade with hidden
138	`__rt` re-export), `mlpl-parity-tests` (parity harness -- nine
139	curated programs run through both paths and agreement is
140	asserted bit-for-bit). Static label mismatches surface as
141	`LowerError::StaticShapeMismatch` which the proc macro converts
142	to `compile_error!`; the `mlpl-build` CLI surfaces them as
143	`mlpl-build: ...` prefixed stderr before cargo is even invoked.
144	Measured 9.05x speedup on a 100x100 reshape+reduce workload
145	(interpreter 479us -> compiled 53us, median of 5). Deferred:
146	`TensorCtor` (`param`/`tensor`), `Repeat`, `Train`, autograd
147	(`grad`), optimizers (`adam`/`momentum_sgd`), and Model DSL
148	(`chain`/`linear`/activations) are all out of compile scope for
149	this saga; they require tape-state or loop lowering. Delivered
150	v0.8. See `docs/milestone-compile-to-rust.md`.
151	
152	## Saga R1: MLX as a Service (COMPLETE)
153	R1 shipped the first concrete backend-service
154	split. `services/mlpl-mlx-serve` is now a separate
155	workspace and service binary for Apple Silicon MLX
156	work, while the main `mlpl-serve` process acts as
157	an orchestrator. The orchestrator accepts
158	`--peer mlx=<url>`, keeps CPU evaluation local,
159	and forwards whole `device("mlx") { ... }` blocks
160	to the peer when one is registered. Peer sessions
161	are created lazily and cached per orchestrator
162	session. The result of a remote device block is an
163	opaque `Value::DeviceTensor { peer, handle, shape,
164	device }`, not copied bytes.
165	
166	The most important user-facing rule is strict
167	materialization: a CPU operation on a peer tensor
168	faults with guidance to call `to_device("cpu", x)`.
169	That explicit fetch path calls the peer transfer
170	endpoint, decodes the f64 tensor envelope, and
171	rebinds the value as a normal local array. The old
172	`to_device(x, "cpu")` spelling remains accepted
173	for compatibility, but the canonical form is
174	`to_device("cpu", x)`.
175	
176	Design deviations from the original services
177	proposal were deliberate. R1 shipped
178	`mlpl-mlx-serve` as its own workspace rather than
179	folding every role into one `mlpl-serve --device`
180	binary; the service already depends on
181	`mlpl-serve` for session and HTTP machinery, so
182	the orchestrator peer helpers duplicate a small
183	wire encode/decode surface for now instead of
184	creating a dependency cycle. If the protocol grows,
185	a tiny shared wire crate is the obvious cleanup.
186	Static `--peer` registration also won over dynamic
187	registration for the first release. Loopback is the
188	safe default, and non-loopback peer URLs require
189	`--insecure-peers` until peer trust and discovery
190	get their own design.
191	
192	The split is a disk-pressure improvement, not a
193	magic shrink. The main `target/` and the service
194	`target/` are independently cleanable and buildable;
195	during release validation the service target sat at
196	about 1 GB while the already-warm main target stayed
197	around 10 GB. That separation matters for the Linux
198	dev-host move and for R2, where CUDA should follow
199	the same service shape instead of entering the main
200	workspace as another in-process optional backend.
201	
202	Shipped artifacts: `demos/mlx_remote.mlpl`,
203	`docs/using-mlx-service.md`, refreshed
204	configuration/status/refactor docs, peer dispatcher
205	tests in `mlpl-eval`, peer routing tests in
206	`mlpl-serve`, and the existing service API / wire
207	tests. Delivered v0.18.0. Next: Saga R2, CUDA as a
208	service, after the Linux + NVIDIA dev host move.

350	sanity-check a planned training run BEFORE committing

358	in the contract -- VRAM sums forward weights +

495	## Saga 15: LoRA Fine-Tuning (COMPLETE)
496	Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for the Model DSL. Three new
497	builtins compose into a PyTorch-`peft`-style "frozen base,
498	trainable low-rank adapters" workflow: `freeze(m)` /
499	`unfreeze(m)` mark every `m.params()` name in a new
500	`env.frozen_params` set that `adam` and `momentum_sgd` skip
501	at the optimizer-update stage (gradient computation is
502	unchanged, so the chain rule still flows through frozen
503	params); `lora(m, rank, alpha, seed)` clones `m`'s spec tree,
504	replaces every `Linear` node with a new `ModelSpec::LinearLora`
505	that owns the cloned base `W`, `b` plus two fresh adapter
506	matrices `A [in, rank]` (init `randn * 1/sqrt(in)`) and
507	`B [rank, out]` (init zeros), and -- after step 004's scope
508	amendment -- auto-freezes EVERY non-adapter param in the
509	student (embed tables, attention projections, and MLP base
510	linears all freeze consistently). The zero-init on B is the
511	standard LoRA "forward identity before training" property:
512	`apply(lora_m, X) == apply(m, X)` elementwise before any
513	gradient step. Forward formula `y = X @ W + (alpha / rank) *
514	X @ A @ B + b` composes through existing matmul / scalar-mul
515	/ add dispatch, so MLX (Saga 14) picks it up for free -- no
516	new tape ops were needed. `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl` trains a
517	Saga 13 Tiny LM on Shakespeare for 100 steps, wraps with
518	rank-8 LoRA, fine-tunes adapters on a synthetic Q/A
519	instruction corpus for 50 steps; base bit-identical
520	throughout, final fine-tune cross-entropy ~2.18.
521	`demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl` is the Apple-Silicon variant
522	with the fine-tune loop under `device("mlx") { }`. A new
523	Criterion bench group `lora_finetune_step` measured warm
524	CPU 164us vs warm MLX 1.11ms = 0.15x (MLX slower at this
525	scale -- LoRA doubles the matmul count per linear and the
526	rank-2 adapter matmuls are too small to amortize MLX's
527	kernel-launch overhead; at d=512 the ratio would flip).
528	CPU-vs-MLX parity across fine-tune losses + every student
529	param (both adapters and frozen base) within 1e-3, pinned
530	by `crates/mlpl-eval/tests/lora_mlx_demo_tests.rs`. A
531	"LoRA Fine-Tuning" web REPL tutorial lesson (tiny V=8, d=4,
532	rank=2 variant) runs interactively in WASM. Delivered
533	v0.13.0. See `docs/using-lora.md` and `docs/benchmarks.md`.

535	## Saga 20: Perturbation research demos / Neural Thickets (COMPLETE)
536	Four new builtins plus a headline demo that compose MLPL into
537	a RandOpt-style weight-perturbation workflow. Seven steps in
538	three phases. Phase 1 shipped the language surface: `clone_model(m)`
539	deep-copies a `ModelSpec` tree and allocates a disjoint set of
540	fresh param names while preserving device tags (step 001);
541	`perturb_params(m, family, sigma, seed)` walks a model's
542	params, filters by one of four families (`all_layers`,
543	`attention_only`, `mlp_only`, `embed_and_head`), and adds
544	`sigma * randn(seed + i, shape)` to each matching param in
545	place, with the "final projection head" detected structurally
546	(the last top-level `Linear` child of the outermost `Chain`,
547	not a name-pattern heuristic) so `mlp_only` / `embed_and_head`
548	can tell MLP linears apart from the vocab projection (step
549	002); `argtop_k(values, k)` returns the k indices of the
550	largest entries in a rank-1 vector (descending by value, ties
551	to lower index; stable sort) and `scatter(buffer, index,
552	value)` returns a copy of a rank-1 buffer with the single
553	entry at `index` replaced by `value` (step 003, both in a
554	new `crates/mlpl-runtime/src/ensemble_builtins.rs`). Phase 2
555	shipped `demos/neural_thicket.mlpl` -- train a Saga 13 Tiny

559	average logits across all 16 variants for an ensemble
560	cross-entropy (step 004, CPU-only; uses `for i in [0,1,2,3]`

609	softmax, transpose, matmul) plus the full `grad(cross_entropy(

636	First saga that proves the platform thesis: a few lines of MLPL

646	numerically-stable `cross_entropy(logits, targets)` over integer
647	targets with max-subtraction log-softmax; `sample(logits, t,
648	seed)` multinomial draws plus `top_k(logits, k)` pre-softmax
649	restriction; and a `last_row` / `concat` / `attention_weights`
650	triple that makes a generation loop and a `[T, T]` attention
651	heatmap one-liner. New demos `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` (end-to-end
652	training) and `demos/tiny_lm_generate.mlpl` (generation +
653	heatmap) wire every Saga 13 primitive together with Saga 12's
654	BPE tokenizer, `shift_pairs_x`/`shift_pairs_y` next-token pair
655	windows, and `experiment "name" { }`-tracked `train N { adam(... )
656	}`. Two new web REPL tutorial lessons -- "Language Model Basics"
657	(forward-only, runs in <2s) and "Training and Generating"
658	(stripped-down training loop + 20-token generation + attention
659	heatmap) -- ship alongside. Delivered v0.10.0. See
660	`docs/milestone-tiny-lm.md`.
661	
662	## Saga 12: Tokenizers, datasets, and experiment tracking (COMPLETE)
663	Closes the last surface-only gap before the Tiny LM. File IO:
664	`load("rel.csv")` / `load("rel.txt")` reads through an
665	`Environment::data_dir` sandbox (terminal REPL `--data-dir`
666	flag); `load_preloaded("name")` serves compiled-in corpora for
667	the web REPL. Dataset prep: `shuffle(x, seed)` Fisher-Yates row
668	permutation, `batch(x, size)` with zero-padded short batches +
669	matching `batch_mask`, `split(x, frac, seed)` and
670	`val_split(x, frac, seed)` returning disjoint chunks; `for row
671	in ds { body }` streaming iteration with `last_rows` capture
672	(new `Token::For`/`Token::In` keywords, `Expr::For` AST
673	variant). Byte-level BPE: `tokenize_bytes` / `decode_bytes`
674	primitives; `Value::Tokenizer` runtime variant with
675	`TokenizerSpec::ByteLevel` and `TokenizerSpec::BpeMerges`;
676	`train_bpe(corpus, vocab_size, seed)` with deterministic
677	lex-smallest tie-breaking; `apply_tokenizer(tok, text)` +
678	`decode(tok, tokens)` byte-lossless round-trip for any UTF-8
679	input. Experiment tracking: `experiment "name" { body }` scoped
680	form captures `_metric`-suffixed scalars and bound params'
681	shapes into `ExperimentRecord`s, logged to
682	`env.experiment_log` and (terminal REPL `--exp-dir`)
683	`<dir>/<name>/<ts>/run.json` via serde_json; `:experiments`
684	REPL command merges memory + disk; `compare(a, b)` builtin
685	returns side-by-side per-metric deltas. Byproduct: lexer UTF-8
686	fix so string literals now carry arbitrary Unicode code points
687	(previously was `b as char` Latin-1 mojibake). Three new
688	tutorial lessons in the web REPL ("Loading Data", "Tokenizing
689	Text", "Experiments"). String-valued variable bindings
690	(`corpus = load_preloaded("...")`) via new
691	`Environment::strings` map. Delivered v0.9.0. See
692	`docs/milestone-tokenizers.md`.

# Saga

## Saga -1: Repo scaffolding (COMPLETE)
Repo compartmentalization scaffolding.

## Saga 0: Foundation (COMPLETE)
Foundation and contracts.

## Saga 1: Dense tensor substrate v1 (COMPLETE)
Shape, DenseArray, reshape, transpose, indexing.

## Saga 2: Parser and evaluator foundation (COMPLETE)
Lexer, AST, parser with precedence, AST-walking evaluator.

## Saga 3: CLI and REPL v1 (COMPLETE)
Working REPL with all v1 syntax, built-in functions, tracing.

## Saga 4: Structured trace v1 (COMPLETE)
TraceEvent/Trace types, evaluator instrumentation, JSON export.

## Saga 5: Visual web viewer v1 (DEFERRED)
Deferred to post-MVP. MVP uses CLI + JSON trace export.

## MVP
Sagas 0 through 4 complete. MVP ships with REPL + trace export.

## Saga 6: ML foundations (COMPLETE)
Sigmoid, tanh_fn, pow, comparison operators, axis reductions, mean,
array constructors (zeros, ones, fill), and the first end-to-end
logistic regression demo. Delivered v0.2.

## Saga 7: SVG visualization v1 (COMPLETE)
`mlpl-viz` crate, `svg(data, type[, aux])` built-in, diagram types
(scatter, line, bar, heatmap, decision_boundary), `grid()` helper,
high-level analysis helpers (hist, scatter_labeled, loss_curve,
confusion_matrix, boundary_2d), browser REPL inline SVG rendering,
and download button. Delivered v0.3.

## Saga 11: Model DSL (COMPLETE)
Composition primitives for neural-net models: a new `Value::Model`
runtime value, atomic `linear(in, out, seed)` layers,
parameter-free activation layers (`tanh_layer`, `relu_layer`,
`softmax_layer`), sequential `chain(...)` composition,
`residual(block)` skip connections, `rms_norm(dim)` normalization,
and `attention(d_model, heads, seed)` multi-head self-attention
(tape-lowered for `heads=1`, forward-only for `heads>1`). A
`params(model)` walker returns the flat parameter list, and
optimizers now accept a model identifier directly so
`adam(loss, mdl, lr, b1, b2, eps)` trains every weight the model
owns through differentiable `apply(mdl, X)`. The v0.6 `moons_mlp`
and `tiny_mlp` demos were rewritten as one-line `chain(...)`
expressions, and a new `transformer_block.mlpl` demo stacks
`residual(chain(rms_norm, attention))` and `residual(chain(
rms_norm, linear, relu_layer, linear))` twice to train a tiny
2-layer transformer block end-to-end (loss 143.87 -> 1.02 over
100 Adam steps, strictly monotonic). New REPL introspection
commands -- `:vars`, `:models`, `:fns`, `:wsid`, `:describe` --
ship in both `mlpl-repl` and `mlpl-web`, and a new "Model
Composition" tutorial lesson walks from a single `linear` through
a chain MLP to Adam inside `train { }` on the moons dataset.
Delivered v0.7. See `docs/milestone-modeldsl.md`.

## Saga 10: Optimizers + training loop (COMPLETE)
Built proper training infrastructure on top of Saga 9 autograd.
New built-ins: `momentum_sgd(loss, params, lr, beta)` and
`adam(loss, params, lr, b1, b2, eps)` with per-parameter state
held in an `OptimizerState` map on the evaluation environment;
`cosine_schedule(step, total, lr_min, lr_max)` and
`linear_warmup(step, warmup, lr)` pure scalar schedules; and
two non-linear synthetic datasets `moons(seed, n, noise)` and
`circles(seed, n, noise)` returning `[N, 3]` `[x, y, label]`
matrices in the same layout as `blobs`. New `train N { body }`
language construct binds the iteration index to `step` inside
the body and captures each iteration's final value into a
`last_losses` 1-D array, replacing the manual
`repeat { grad; manual update; record loss }` recipe. Two new
demos -- `demos/moons_mlp.mlpl` and `demos/circles_mlp.mlpl` --
train a tanh MLP with `adam` inside `train { }` and render the
decision boundary with `boundary_2d`. New "Optimizers and
Schedules" tutorial lesson added to the web REPL. Delivered v0.6.

## Saga 9: Autograd v1 (COMPLETE)
Reverse-mode autograd as a language primitive. New `mlpl-autograd`
crate provides a tape-based `Tensor` with backward over add, sub,
mul, div, neg, exp, log, relu, tanh, sigmoid, softmax, sum, mean,
transpose, reshape, and matmul, all gradcheck-verified against
finite differences. Parser surface adds `param[shape]` and
`tensor[shape]` constructors, and a new `grad(expr, wrt)` built-in
lifts array expressions onto the tape and returns the gradient
with respect to a tracked parameter. The v0.4 `tiny_mlp` and
`softmax_classifier` demos were ported to use `param + grad`
instead of hand-written backprop, and a new "Automatic
Differentiation" tutorial lesson walks from a scalar minimization
to a one-layer linear regression. Delivered v0.5.

## Saga 8: ML demos (COMPLETE)
Synthetic data primitives (random, randn, argmax, blobs) and
higher-level ML built-ins (softmax, one_hot), plus six demos wired
into the browser REPL: k-means clustering, PCA via power iteration,
a linear softmax classifier, a tiny MLP on XOR-style data, and a
scaled dot-product attention pattern. Tutorial lessons added for
each. Delivered v0.4.

## Saga 11.5: Named Axes and shape introspection (COMPLETE)
Axis-labeled shapes threaded through `Value::Array` via a new
`LabeledShape` type on `mlpl-core`. `label(x, [...])` and `relabel(x,
[...])` primitives, annotation syntax on assignment (`x : [batch,
time, dim] = ...`), and `reshape_labeled(x, dims, labels)` as the
opt-in re-labeling path. Label propagation through elementwise
ops (with one-None-one-Some accepted and mismatches rejected),
matmul (contraction axis validated, outer dims passed through),
reduce/argmax (reduced axis's label dropped), and `map()`
(preserves labels through every math builtin). `reduce_add`,
`reduce_mul`, `argmax`, and `softmax` accept an axis name string
in place of an integer. Structured `EvalError::ShapeMismatch
{ op, expected: LabeledShape, actual: LabeledShape }` at the
evaluator boundary, with Display rendering as `op: expected
[seq=N, d=M], got [time=N, d=M]`. Label-aware `:vars` and
`:describe` (using `LabeledShape` Display), and trace JSON that
round-trips axis labels for labeled arrays and omits the key
entirely for unlabeled ones. New "Named Axes" tutorial lesson in
the web REPL; "Model Composition" lesson now annotates X as
`[batch, feat]` so labels flow through `apply(mdl, X)`. Delivered
v0.7.5. See `docs/milestone-named-axes.md`.

## Saga: Compile-to-Rust (COMPLETE)
Lowers MLPL source to Rust `TokenStream` shared by three targets:
the `mlpl!` proc macro (compile-time embed inside Rust apps), the
`mlpl build foo.mlpl -o bin` subcommand (native-binary and
cross-compile via cargo+rustc, verified for native and
wasm32-unknown-unknown), and a leaner future WASM path that
reuses the same pipeline. New crates: `mlpl-rt` (runtime target;
typed primitive wrappers around `DenseArray`/`LabeledShape`),
`mlpl-lower-rs` (AST -> `TokenStream` with path-configurable
runtime prefix and static matmul contraction checks when both
operands' labels are known at lower time), `mlpl-macro`
(proc-macro wrapper), `mlpl` (user-facing facade with hidden
`__rt` re-export), `mlpl-parity-tests` (parity harness -- nine
curated programs run through both paths and agreement is
asserted bit-for-bit). Static label mismatches surface as
`LowerError::StaticShapeMismatch` which the proc macro converts
to `compile_error!`; the `mlpl-build` CLI surfaces them as
`mlpl-build: ...` prefixed stderr before cargo is even invoked.
Measured 9.05x speedup on a 100x100 reshape+reduce workload
(interpreter 479us -> compiled 53us, median of 5). Deferred:
`TensorCtor` (`param`/`tensor`), `Repeat`, `Train`, autograd
(`grad`), optimizers (`adam`/`momentum_sgd`), and Model DSL
(`chain`/`linear`/activations) are all out of compile scope for
this saga; they require tape-state or loop lowering. Delivered
v0.8. See `docs/milestone-compile-to-rust.md`.

## Saga R1: MLX as a Service (COMPLETE)
R1 shipped the first concrete backend-service
split. `services/mlpl-mlx-serve` is now a separate
workspace and service binary for Apple Silicon MLX
work, while the main `mlpl-serve` process acts as
an orchestrator. The orchestrator accepts
`--peer mlx=<url>`, keeps CPU evaluation local,
and forwards whole `device("mlx") { ... }` blocks
to the peer when one is registered. Peer sessions
are created lazily and cached per orchestrator
session. The result of a remote device block is an
opaque `Value::DeviceTensor { peer, handle, shape,
device }`, not copied bytes.

The most important user-facing rule is strict
materialization: a CPU operation on a peer tensor
faults with guidance to call `to_device("cpu", x)`.
That explicit fetch path calls the peer transfer
endpoint, decodes the f64 tensor envelope, and
rebinds the value as a normal local array. The old
`to_device(x, "cpu")` spelling remains accepted
for compatibility, but the canonical form is
`to_device("cpu", x)`.

Design deviations from the original services
proposal were deliberate. R1 shipped
`mlpl-mlx-serve` as its own workspace rather than
folding every role into one `mlpl-serve --device`
binary; the service already depends on
`mlpl-serve` for session and HTTP machinery, so
the orchestrator peer helpers duplicate a small
wire encode/decode surface for now instead of
creating a dependency cycle. If the protocol grows,
a tiny shared wire crate is the obvious cleanup.
Static `--peer` registration also won over dynamic
registration for the first release. Loopback is the
safe default, and non-loopback peer URLs require
`--insecure-peers` until peer trust and discovery
get their own design.

The split is a disk-pressure improvement, not a
magic shrink. The main `target/` and the service
`target/` are independently cleanable and buildable;
during release validation the service target sat at
about 1 GB while the already-warm main target stayed
around 10 GB. That separation matters for the Linux
dev-host move and for R2, where CUDA should follow
the same service shape instead of entering the main
workspace as another in-process optional backend.

Shipped artifacts: `demos/mlx_remote.mlpl`,
`docs/using-mlx-service.md`, refreshed
configuration/status/refactor docs, peer dispatcher
tests in `mlpl-eval`, peer routing tests in
`mlpl-serve`, and the existing service API / wire
tests. Delivered v0.18.0. Next: Saga R2, CUDA as a
service, after the Linux + NVIDIA dev host move.

## Saga 21: CLI Server + Multi-Client UI (MVP) (COMPLETE)
First piece of the multi-client story: a long-
running MLPL interpreter exposed as a REST server
(`crates/mlpl-serve`), a thin CLI client
(`mlpl-repl --connect <url>`), and a content-
addressed CLI visualization cache
(`MLPL_CACHE_DIR`) that finally stops the terminal
from dumping raw `<svg>` XML. Three new packages,
four new contracts, one new retrospective doc. The
server skeleton (auth.rs / sessions.rs /
handlers.rs / server.rs / main.rs, each under the
7-fn cap) ships `POST /v1/sessions` (no auth, hands
out a 32-char alphanumeric bearer token),
`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/eval` (auth required;
lex+parse+`eval_program_value` against the
session's `Environment`; returns
`{value, kind}`), `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/inspect`
(auth required; structured workspace snapshot --
vars sorted+capped at 200 with `more` count, models
/ tokenizers / experiments sorted+deduped), and
`GET /v1/health`. Constant-time token compare via
`subtle::ConstantTimeEq`; `--bind 0.0.0.0` (or any
non-loopback) refuses to start under
`--auth disabled`. axum 0.7 + tokio + tower stack.
The `mlpl-repl --connect <url>` client splits
between `connect.rs` (HTTP transport: 4 fns) and
`connect_repl.rs` (REPL loop + slash dispatch +
`--connect` argv parser: 4 fns) -- two modules
because connect.rs would have hit the 7-fn cap
otherwise. Local `Environment` is unused in connect
mode; slash commands `:vars` / `:models` /
`:tokenizers` / `:experiments` / `:wsid` go through
`/inspect`, while `:ask` keeps using
`mlpl_runtime::call_ollama` directly (server-side
framing follows in a future saga). `--connect` is
incompatible with `-f` / `--data-dir` / `--exp-dir`
(parser errors with exit code 2). The CLI viz
cache lives at `crates/mlpl-cli/src/viz_cache.rs`:
SHA-256-prefix-12 chars under
`$MLPL_CACHE_DIR` / `dirs::cache_dir().join("mlpl")`,
with content-addressed naming so identical viz
outputs don't duplicate; non-SVG values pass
through. Wired into both local `eval_line` and
connect-mode `read_loop`. `svg_out.rs` simplified
from the previous SVG handler to a thin holder for
the `--svg-out <dir>` back-compat override flag.
35 new tests across the saga (13 server +
4 connect + 18 viz_cache); sw-checklist baseline
139 fails held throughout. Hit two budget walls
during impl -- connect.rs at 8 fns split into
connect.rs + connect_repl.rs; main.rs's `main` fn
at 58 LOC compressed via a local closure for the
flag-lookup pattern (couldn't extract a top-level
helper because main.rs was already at the 7-fn
cap). `docs/using-cli-server.md` is the user-
facing retrospective; `docs/configurations.md`
refreshed with new rows + footnote [8] explicitly
distinguishing "MVP shipped" from "LLM-proxy
follow-up still deferred." Carved out as
post-MVP and listed in the deferred non-goals:
the server-side LLM proxy with allow-list
(unblocks browser `llm_call`; needs a security
review for allow-list + secret handling first),
visualization storage URLs, Server-Sent-Events
streaming, cancellation, persistence across
restarts, web UI re-routing to call origin,
reattach across REPL restarts, the WebSocket
surface, the desktop GUI wrapper (tauri / wry),
the Emacs client, the ratatui TUI client, and
other viz formats (PNG / HTML / JSON). Each lands
in a follow-up saga after the MVP server contract
proves stable. Delivered v0.17.0. R1 followed by
turning MLX into a peer service; next service work
is the dev host move to Linux + NVIDIA, then R2
(CUDA as a service).

## Saga 19: LLM-as-Tool REST Integration (COMPLETE)
A language-level builtin that POSTs to an Ollama-
compatible `/api/generate` endpoint and returns the
model's completion text as a `Value::Str` scalar.
The REPL's preview `:ask` command (shipped in
v0.11.x as the Saga 19 preview) predated this; it
now delegates to the same `mlpl_runtime::call_ollama`
path so the HTTP machinery lives in one place. The
headline use case is "LLM as a tool" -- pipe a value
through a hosted LLM, store the reply as an MLPL
string, feed it to `tokenize_bytes` /
`experiment {}` / the rest of the pipeline. The
language surface is exactly `llm_call(url, prompt,
model) -> string`: URL is normalized (trailing
slashes stripped, `/api/generate` appended unless
already present, no double-append), 120-second
timeout matches the `:ask` preview, returns the
top-level `response` field as a string. Non-2xx
status, invalid JSON, or missing `response` field
all surface as actionable errors carrying
`"llm_call"`, the URL, and a 200-character body
preview. CLI-only -- the browser cannot reach
localhost Ollama without CORS allow-listing + a
server-side proxy; that path lands in Saga 21
(`mlpl-serve`). Module layout splits the pure HTTP
path (`crates/mlpl-runtime/src/llm_builtins.rs`, 3
fns) from the `Expr`-aware dispatch shim
(`crates/mlpl-eval/src/llm_dispatch.rs`, 1 fn) --
mirrors Saga 22's revised layout. **Design
deviation** from the original step 001 plan, which
proposed 5 functions in the runtime crate
(try_call / builtin_llm_call / validate_args /
resolve_url / parse_response): try_call and
validate_args need `Expr` access that the runtime
crate intentionally avoids, so they moved to the
eval-side dispatcher. The :ask migration is a
**behavior change**: the pre-v0.16 :ask used
Ollama's `/api/chat` with explicit
`{role: system}` + `{role: user}` messages; the
new :ask concatenates the same content into a
single prompt and POSTs to `/api/generate`. Model
loses the role distinction but keeps the context;
TODO note in `apps/mlpl-repl/src/ask.rs` flags a
future `llm_chat(history, prompt)` variant (listed
in step 001's deferred non-goals) as the path to
restore `/api/chat` semantics. 8 mockito-based
integration tests pin the URL-resolution +
arity + error catalog. New `demos/llm_tool.mlpl`
exercises `llm_call` -> `tokenize_bytes`
end-to-end (verified live during step 002 against
a running local Ollama). `docs/using-llm-tool.md`
is the user guide; `docs/using-ollama.md` was
updated to redirect to it; `docs/configurations.md`
gained an `llm_call` row + footnote [7]. Streaming
SSE, OpenAI-style tool calling, multi-turn chat,
request batching, in-source auth secrets,
teacher-model distillation pipelines, and
web / WASM support all stay deferred -- see the
contract for the full list. sw-checklist baseline
102/139 held across both feature steps. Delivered
v0.16.0. Saga 21 (CLI server) is next.

## Saga 22: Feasibility Checking + Resource Estimation (COMPLETE)
Four new language-level builtins that let the user
sanity-check a planned training run BEFORE committing
disk, RAM, and hours of wall-clock to it. Pure math
over a `ModelSpec` (or a hardcoded HF-scale dimension
table) plus train-loop parameters; no weights required
for what-if queries. `estimate_train(model, steps,
batch_size, seq_len [, dtype_bytes])` returns a
rank-1 `[5]` f64 array `[params, vram_bytes,
disk_bytes, flops, wall_seconds]` with labels pinned
in the contract -- VRAM sums forward weights +
gradient + Adam m/v moments (trainable only; LoRA
frozen base is zero on the grad/adam legs) + a `4x`
activation safety factor; FLOPS covers Linear /
LinearLora / Attention / Embedding; wall-clock reads
throughput from a cached env key defaulting to 50
GFLOPS (CPU laptop lower bound). `calibrate_device()`
runs a 10-iteration 1024x1024 matmul benchmark
through `device::dispatched_call` (first iter is
warmup), measures wall-clock, writes observed GFLOPS
into `mlpl_device_throughput_gflops`; device-aware
under `device("mlx") { }` so subsequent estimates on
that device read honest numbers.
`estimate_hypothetical(name, ...)` talks about
SmolLM-135M / 360M / 1.7B / Llama-3.2-1B /
Qwen-2.5-0.5B via a hardcoded dimension table --
**design deviation from the original plan**, which
proposed `hypothetical_model(name) -> ModelSpec` that
`estimate_train` would walk. That path required
materializing zero arrays in `env` for every
parameter in the spec, and a SmolLM-1.7B query would
have cost ~14 GB of RAM just to ask the question.
Shipped as a direct `[5]`-return builtin instead; the
output shape is identical to `estimate_train` so
`feasible(...)` composes unchanged.
`feasible(estimate_result, budget)` takes the `[5]`
estimate plus a `[3]` `[vram, disk, wall]` budget
(zeros skip that dimension) and returns scalar 1/0
for `if feasible(est, [4e9, 1e10, 600]) { train ... }`
guards. 23 new tests (11 estimate + 12 feasibility;
one ignored for the slow default-size calibrate
bench). Two contracts for step 001
(`contracts/eval-contract/estimate.md`) plus three
for step 002 (`calibrate-device.md`,
`estimate-hypothetical.md`, `feasible.md`). Module
layout: `crates/mlpl-runtime/src/estimate_builtins.rs`
(6 fns) + `crates/mlpl-eval/src/model_feasibility.rs`
(7 fns at limit); sw-checklist baseline 102/139 held
across both steps. `demos/feasibility.mlpl` tours
all four builtins end-to-end (CLI-only because
browser timers are too noisy for calibration).
`docs/using-feasibility.md` retrospective + user
guide documents the estimator math, the ~2x
accuracy target, the hardcoded HF-scale table, the
LoRA-on-SmolLM worked example, the guard pattern,
and the deferred non-goals (HF download +
safetensors loading, f16/bf16 tensor support,
dynamic profiling, distributed / multi-GPU, auto-
recovery). Delivered v0.15.0. Saga 19 (LLM-as-tool
REST `llm_call`) is next.

## Saga 16: Embedding Visualization (COMPLETE)
Embedding-inspection surface for any model with an
`embed` layer or any rank-2 `[N, D]` intermediate
representation. Three new builtins plus one new viz
type close the "train a model, inspect what it
learned" loop: `pairwise_sqdist(X)` returns the
`[N, N]` squared-Euclidean distance matrix with
symmetry + zero-diagonal + empty-input safety;
`knn(X, k)` returns each row's k nearest non-self
neighbors sorted by ascending distance with lower-
index tie-break (self never appears in its own row);
`tsne(X, perplexity, iters, seed)` runs classic van
der Maaten t-SNE to produce `[N, 2]` with per-row
perplexity-calibrated binary search, symmetrized
joint probabilities, Student-t low-dim affinities,
momentum-based KL-gradient descent with early
exaggeration, deterministic under identical seeds.
`svg(pts, "scatter3d")` renders `[N, 3]` (point
cloud) or `[N, 4]` (points + integer cluster id) as
a static orthographic-projection SVG with labeled
axis gizmos + one `<circle>` per point + optional
sorted legend. `demos/embedding_viz.mlpl` composes
the pipeline end-to-end: train a standalone
`embed(12, 8, 0)` toward a structured 3-cluster
target via MSE for 50 adam steps; extract the
learned table via `apply(emb, iota(V))`; render
through t-SNE + column-selector + `knn` to show that
learned embeddings recover the target structure
(every token's nearest neighbors stay in its own
cluster). 35 tests across five files pin every
invariant. The t-SNE builtin was first written as a
300-line monolith (three new sw-checklist FAILs);
user feedback paused the work to document the
decomposition rules, producing
`docs/sw-checklist-patterns.md` (catalog of struct-
return, struct-args, validate-then-work, orchestrator
+ helpers, phase helpers, extract-to-module, chain-
of-responsibility, bridge, split-tests-from-work
patterns with worked examples from this codebase).
The monolith was then split into four sibling modules
(`tsne_builtin` / `tsne_validate` / `tsne_affinities`
/ `tsne_gradient`), each a single-responsibility
facade under every budget; baseline 139/102 sw-
checklist held. PCA stays a composition pattern (the
Saga 8 power-iteration + deflation lesson) rather
than shipping a new builtin. t-SNE itself is CPU-only
(inner loop does not vectorize cleanly through MLX).
UMAP, RAG pipeline (pending Saga 19), interactive
3-D, MLX for tsne, Barnes-Hut approximate t-SNE all
deferred; see `docs/using-embeddings.md` "Not
shipped". Delivered v0.14.0.

### Addendum: Saga 16.5 -- Embedding-viz Polish (COMPLETE)

Two convenience builtins that closed the Saga 16 loose
ends flagged in the shipped `docs/using-embeddings.md`
"Not shipped" list: `pca(X, k) -> Y [N, k]` wraps
power iteration + Gram-Schmidt + deflation into a
one-liner (the Gram-Schmidt-inside-power-iteration
step is load-bearing for `k = D` on rank-deficient
inputs where plain deflation lets `v` drift back
toward earlier components), and `embed_table(model) ->
[vocab, d_model]` walks a `ModelSpec` tree depth-
first left-to-right and returns the first Embedding
layer's lookup table cloned from `env` (first-match
semantics; Chain / Residual / nested chain all
traverse; no-Embedding errors cleanly). 17 new tests
(9 pca + 8 embed_table), both modules under the 7-fn
budget by design (6 and 2 respectively), sw-checklist
baseline 139/102 held. `demos/embedding_viz.mlpl`
now uses `pca(table, 3)` for the 3-D projection
(principled instead of the first-three-dims selector
shortcut). `docs/using-embeddings.md` rewrites the
PCA section from "composition-only" to "shipped as a
builtin in v0.14.1" (keeps the power-iteration recipe
as pedagogy), adds an "Extracting embed-layer
weights" section, and updates the "Training inside a
chain" flow to use `embed_table(m)` instead of the
`apply(standalone_embed, iota(V))` workaround. Web
REPL "Embedding exploration" lesson adds `pca(X, 2)`
and `embed_table(emb)` examples. Path-selector
variants of `embed_table` (e.g., `embed_table(m,
"encoder.embed")`), multi-embedding stacks, and
streaming / randomized / kernel PCA all deferred.
Delivered v0.14.1. In-family polish, not a full saga.

## Saga 15: LoRA Fine-Tuning (COMPLETE)
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for the Model DSL. Three new
builtins compose into a PyTorch-`peft`-style "frozen base,
trainable low-rank adapters" workflow: `freeze(m)` /
`unfreeze(m)` mark every `m.params()` name in a new
`env.frozen_params` set that `adam` and `momentum_sgd` skip
at the optimizer-update stage (gradient computation is
unchanged, so the chain rule still flows through frozen
params); `lora(m, rank, alpha, seed)` clones `m`'s spec tree,
replaces every `Linear` node with a new `ModelSpec::LinearLora`
that owns the cloned base `W`, `b` plus two fresh adapter
matrices `A [in, rank]` (init `randn * 1/sqrt(in)`) and
`B [rank, out]` (init zeros), and -- after step 004's scope
amendment -- auto-freezes EVERY non-adapter param in the
student (embed tables, attention projections, and MLP base
linears all freeze consistently). The zero-init on B is the
standard LoRA "forward identity before training" property:
`apply(lora_m, X) == apply(m, X)` elementwise before any
gradient step. Forward formula `y = X @ W + (alpha / rank) *
X @ A @ B + b` composes through existing matmul / scalar-mul
/ add dispatch, so MLX (Saga 14) picks it up for free -- no
new tape ops were needed. `demos/lora_finetune.mlpl` trains a
Saga 13 Tiny LM on Shakespeare for 100 steps, wraps with
rank-8 LoRA, fine-tunes adapters on a synthetic Q/A
instruction corpus for 50 steps; base bit-identical
throughout, final fine-tune cross-entropy ~2.18.
`demos/lora_finetune_mlx.mlpl` is the Apple-Silicon variant
with the fine-tune loop under `device("mlx") { }`. A new
Criterion bench group `lora_finetune_step` measured warm
CPU 164us vs warm MLX 1.11ms = 0.15x (MLX slower at this
scale -- LoRA doubles the matmul count per linear and the
rank-2 adapter matmuls are too small to amortize MLX's
kernel-launch overhead; at d=512 the ratio would flip).
CPU-vs-MLX parity across fine-tune losses + every student
param (both adapters and frozen base) within 1e-3, pinned
by `crates/mlpl-eval/tests/lora_mlx_demo_tests.rs`. A
"LoRA Fine-Tuning" web REPL tutorial lesson (tiny V=8, d=4,
rank=2 variant) runs interactively in WASM. Delivered
v0.13.0. See `docs/using-lora.md` and `docs/benchmarks.md`.

## Saga 20: Perturbation research demos / Neural Thickets (COMPLETE)
Four new builtins plus a headline demo that compose MLPL into
a RandOpt-style weight-perturbation workflow. Seven steps in
three phases. Phase 1 shipped the language surface: `clone_model(m)`
deep-copies a `ModelSpec` tree and allocates a disjoint set of
fresh param names while preserving device tags (step 001);
`perturb_params(m, family, sigma, seed)` walks a model's
params, filters by one of four families (`all_layers`,
`attention_only`, `mlp_only`, `embed_and_head`), and adds
`sigma * randn(seed + i, shape)` to each matching param in
place, with the "final projection head" detected structurally
(the last top-level `Linear` child of the outermost `Chain`,
not a name-pattern heuristic) so `mlp_only` / `embed_and_head`
can tell MLP linears apart from the vocab projection (step
002); `argtop_k(values, k)` returns the k indices of the
largest entries in a rank-1 vector (descending by value, ties
to lower index; stable sort) and `scatter(buffer, index,
value)` returns a copy of a rank-1 buffer with the single
entry at `index` replaced by `value` (step 003, both in a
new `crates/mlpl-runtime/src/ensemble_builtins.rs`). Phase 2
shipped `demos/neural_thicket.mlpl` -- train a Saga 13 Tiny
LM base, sweep 4 families x 4 seeds = 16 variants, score
each on a held-out string, render a `[family x seed]`
specialization heatmap, pick top-K via `argtop_k`, and
average logits across all 16 variants for an ensemble
cross-entropy (step 004, CPU-only; uses `for i in [0,1,2,3]`
loops per family because `repeat` does not expose a counter
and MLPL lacks string-array indexing for `families[i/4]`).
`demos/neural_thicket_mlx.mlpl` wraps the variant loop +
ensemble in a single `device("mlx") { ... }` block (base
training stays on CPU); losses and ensemble logits agree
with the CPU path elementwise within fp32 tolerance, pinned
by a triple-gated integration test (step 005). A new
`mlpl-bench` Criterion group `neural_thicket_variant_loop`
measures warm CPU 767us vs warm MLX 3.01ms (MLX 0.25x), a
ratio essentially identical to Saga 14's 0.26x on
`tiny_lm_train_step` -- evidence that the bottleneck at
Tiny LM inner dimensions is per-op kernel launch + f32
round-trip, not autograd-specific cost. Phase 3 shipped a
"Neural Thickets" web REPL tutorial lesson (tiny 4x4 sweep
at V=8/d=4 so the full heatmap renders in the browser),
`docs/using-perturbation.md` (retrospective covering the
four builtins, the four families, the heatmap narrative,
measured MLX numbers, and the deferred follow-up surface:
depth-aware families / low-rank perturbation / real
checkpoints / strict top-K ensembling / `repeat`
step-counter), and rebuilt `pages/` for the live demo
(step 006). Delivered v0.12.0. See
`docs/mlpl-for-neural-thickets.md` for the design sketch and
`docs/using-perturbation.md` for the shipped-surface doc.

## Saga 14: MLX backend (COMPLETE)
First accelerator backend for MLPL: a program that trains on CPU
now runs on Apple Silicon via MLX without source changes. Ten
steps across five phases. Phase 1 built a `crates/mlpl-mlx`
sibling to `mlpl-rt` with MLX-backed equivalents of every
forward primitive the Tiny LM touches (matmul, add/sub/mul/div/
neg, exp/log/tanh/sigmoid/relu, reshape/transpose, reduce_mul/
mean/argmax axis-aware, softmax/log_softmax, fused
cross_entropy), each parity-tested vs CPU within documented
fp32 tolerance. Phase 2 added the `device("mlx") { body }`
scoped form in the parser/AST (mirroring `experiment`'s shape),
the `to_device(x, target)` movement helper (also walks the
param tree for models), cross-device-safety as a typed
`EvalError::DeviceMismatch { op, expected, actual }` variant,
and routed every Saga 11 model's forward (`linear`, `chain`,
`residual`, `rms_norm`, `attention`, `causal_attention`,
`embed`, activations) through a single `dispatched_call`
helper. Phase 3 wired autograd on MLX: `grad(expr, wrt)` inside
a `device("mlx") { }` block re-materializes the CPU-built tape's
forward values through `mlpl-mlx` before CPU backward formulas
compute gradients, producing gradients that match the all-CPU
path within fp32 tolerance across every tape primitive (sum,
mean, exp, log, relu, tanh, sigmoid, neg, add, mul, div,
softmax, transpose, matmul) plus the full `grad(cross_entropy(
apply(model, X), Y), W)` integration path. Adam, momentum_sgd,
`train N { body }`, `last_losses`, `cosine_schedule`,
`linear_warmup`, and `experiment "name" { body }` all inherit
from the grad wiring and produce parameter updates and loss
curves that match CPU on a Tiny LM-shaped slice within 1e-4.
Phase 4 shipped `demos/tiny_lm_mlx.mlpl` (the Saga 13 body
wrapped in `device("mlx") { }`, identical seeds, hyperparams,
dataset, 200 steps, loss curve matches CPU) and extended
`mlpl-bench` with a Criterion harness comparing CPU vs MLX on
`reshape_reduce_100x100` and a `tiny_lm_train_step` workload,
reporting both cold and warm wall-clock timings. Phase 5 added
a "Running on MLX" web REPL tutorial lesson, turned
`docs/using-mlx.md` from design sketch into shipped-API
reference with a retrospective, and rebuilt the live demo page.
Measured performance at Tiny LM scale: MLX is 0.84x on
reshape+reduce and 0.26x on the training step -- below the saga
plan's 5x warm-path gate. Four bottlenecks diagnosed in
`docs/benchmarks.md` (f32/f64 round-trip per op, no graph
fusion, tape re-materialization doubles forward work, d=16/32
inner dims dominated by kernel-launch overhead); a dedicated
"MLX throughput" follow-up step is the natural next work item.
Correctness is intact -- every MLX-gated parity test across
the saga passes. Delivered v0.11.0. See
`docs/milestone-mlx-backend.md` and `docs/using-mlx.md`.

## Saga 13: Tiny language model end-to-end (COMPLETE)
First saga that proves the platform thesis: a few lines of MLPL
train a small transformer LM, generate text from a prompt, and
render the attention pattern -- all on CPU, all reproducible via
experiment tracking. Six new primitives filled the gap between
Saga 12's tokenizer surface and a working LM: `embed(vocab,
d_model, seed)` as a `Value::Model` with a learned `[vocab,
d_model]` table and gradient flow; deterministic
`sinusoidal_encoding(T, d_model)` additive positional tables;
`causal_attention(d_model, heads, seed)` with a lower-triangular
pre-softmax mask so position `t` cannot peek at `t+1`;
numerically-stable `cross_entropy(logits, targets)` over integer
targets with max-subtraction log-softmax; `sample(logits, t,
seed)` multinomial draws plus `top_k(logits, k)` pre-softmax
restriction; and a `last_row` / `concat` / `attention_weights`
triple that makes a generation loop and a `[T, T]` attention
heatmap one-liner. New demos `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` (end-to-end
training) and `demos/tiny_lm_generate.mlpl` (generation +
heatmap) wire every Saga 13 primitive together with Saga 12's
BPE tokenizer, `shift_pairs_x`/`shift_pairs_y` next-token pair
windows, and `experiment "name" { }`-tracked `train N { adam(... )
}`. Two new web REPL tutorial lessons -- "Language Model Basics"
(forward-only, runs in <2s) and "Training and Generating"
(stripped-down training loop + 20-token generation + attention
heatmap) -- ship alongside. Delivered v0.10.0. See
`docs/milestone-tiny-lm.md`.

## Saga 12: Tokenizers, datasets, and experiment tracking (COMPLETE)
Closes the last surface-only gap before the Tiny LM. File IO:
`load("rel.csv")` / `load("rel.txt")` reads through an
`Environment::data_dir` sandbox (terminal REPL `--data-dir`
flag); `load_preloaded("name")` serves compiled-in corpora for
the web REPL. Dataset prep: `shuffle(x, seed)` Fisher-Yates row
permutation, `batch(x, size)` with zero-padded short batches +
matching `batch_mask`, `split(x, frac, seed)` and
`val_split(x, frac, seed)` returning disjoint chunks; `for row
in ds { body }` streaming iteration with `last_rows` capture
(new `Token::For`/`Token::In` keywords, `Expr::For` AST
variant). Byte-level BPE: `tokenize_bytes` / `decode_bytes`
primitives; `Value::Tokenizer` runtime variant with
`TokenizerSpec::ByteLevel` and `TokenizerSpec::BpeMerges`;
`train_bpe(corpus, vocab_size, seed)` with deterministic
lex-smallest tie-breaking; `apply_tokenizer(tok, text)` +
`decode(tok, tokens)` byte-lossless round-trip for any UTF-8
input. Experiment tracking: `experiment "name" { body }` scoped
form captures `_metric`-suffixed scalars and bound params'
shapes into `ExperimentRecord`s, logged to
`env.experiment_log` and (terminal REPL `--exp-dir`)
`<dir>/<name>/<ts>/run.json` via serde_json; `:experiments`
REPL command merges memory + disk; `compare(a, b)` builtin
returns side-by-side per-metric deltas. Byproduct: lexer UTF-8
fix so string literals now carry arbitrary Unicode code points
(previously was `b as char` Latin-1 mojibake). Three new
tutorial lessons in the web REPL ("Loading Data", "Tokenizing
Text", "Experiments"). String-valued variable bindings
(`corpus = load_preloaded("...")`) via new
`Environment::strings` map. Delivered v0.9.0. See
`docs/milestone-tokenizers.md`.

ratatui / Emacs / desktop GUI clients) fold into a

contract proves stable in real use; not gated on
the Linux move.

1	# Typed ML Concepts (design proposal)
2	
3	**Status:** design proposal, not yet a saga. Captures the
4	"typing assistance for ML concepts" direction the user asked
5	about on 2026-04-09 after the v0.7.0 release. Intended to seed
6	a future Saga (call it 11.7 or 12.5 depending on dependency
7	ordering).
8	
9	For the current typing model, see `docs/typing.md`. For the
10	inserted Saga 11.5 that adds labeled axes (a prerequisite for
11	some of this), see `docs/milestone-named-axes.md`.
12	
13	## Why types for ML concepts?
14	
15	MLPL today represents the entire ML world as `DenseArray` plus
16	the model DSL's `ModelSpec`. That is enough to *run* a model,
17	but it is not enough to *talk about* one. The user (human or
18	agent) cannot ask:
19	
20	- "What kind of layer is this?"
21	- "Is this tensor a weight, a gradient, an input, or an
22	  activation?"
23	- "Which layers in this chain produce hidden states I might want
24	  to inspect?"
25	- "Which parameters belong to the encoder vs the decoder?"
26	- "Is this number a learning rate or a temperature?"
27	
28	Answers to these questions exist *in the user's head* and *in
29	naming conventions* but not in the language. Adding semantic
30	types to ML concepts would let the language carry that meaning,
31	expose it via `:describe`, validate it at op boundaries, and
32	give agents a structured surface to reason against.
33	
34	This document is a sketch of what such a type system could look
35	like, what concepts deserve to be typed first, and what stages
36	of adoption are feasible without rewriting the language.
37	
38	## What "type" means in this proposal
39	
40	Three different things, layered:
41	
42	1. **Tags** -- a runtime label attached to a `DenseArray` that
43	   says "this is a weight" or "this is a hidden activation".
44	   Carried in the value, used by `:describe` and by error
45	   messages, validated only when an op explicitly asks. Cheap.
46	2. **Roles** -- a structured tag with extra fields. A `Weight`
47	   role might carry its layer name, its position in the layer
48	   (e.g. `W` vs `b`), and its initializer seed. A
49	   `LearningRate` role might carry its schedule.
50	3. **Interfaces** -- a contract on what a value supports. A
51	   `Layer` interface promises `apply(layer, X)` works and
52	   advertises its expected input and output shapes. An
53	   `Optimizer` interface promises a `step(params, grad)` style
54	   call.
55	
56	Tags are the cheapest to add and the most user-visible. Roles
57	build on tags. Interfaces are the largest jump because they
58	require dispatch on the role at the call site.
59	
60	This proposal recommends starting with **tags**, opportunistically
61	upgrading hot ones to **roles** as concrete demos require it,
62	and deferring **interfaces** until a future saga (likely
63	post-Saga 11.5 named axes, since interfaces want shape labels
64	to be useful).
65	
66	## ML concepts that deserve a type
67	
68	In rough order of payoff per unit of language complexity.
69	
70	### Tier A: ship first
71	
72	These are the concepts where the lack of typing already hurts
73	demo readability and `:describe` output today.
74	
75	| Concept            | Today                                  | Proposed type tag       | Why                                                                |
76	|--------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
77	| **Weight**         | a `DenseArray` marked as a `param`     | `Weight { layer, name }` | distinguish trainable matrices from data tensors and from biases   |
78	| **Bias**           | a `DenseArray` marked as a `param`     | `Bias { layer }`         | same distinction; biases initialize differently and rarely decay   |
79	| **Input**          | a `DenseArray` you happen to pass to `apply` | `Input { kind }`     | enable shape and label checks against a layer's expected input     |
80	| **Output / logits** | a `DenseArray` returned by `apply`     | `Output { layer }`       | mark predictions for downstream loss/eval consumers                |
81	| **Hidden activation** | an intermediate `DenseArray` from `tanh_layer`/`relu_layer` | `Activation { layer, kind }` | makes "where is the hidden state from layer 3?" answerable |
82	| **Loss**           | a scalar `DenseArray` named "loss"     | `Loss { kind }`          | distinguish MSE / cross-entropy / KL for `:describe` and reporting |
83	| **Gradient**       | the result of `grad(loss, w)`          | `Gradient { wrt }`       | trace which param a gradient belongs to without naming convention  |
84	| **Learning rate**  | a scalar `DenseArray` named "lr"       | `LearningRate { schedule }` | catch mistakes like passing an array where a scalar lr is expected |
85	| **Label vector**   | an integer-valued `DenseArray`         | `Labels { num_classes }` | allow `confusion_matrix` to validate matching class counts         |
86	
87	These are all *additive*: every concept already exists as a
88	`DenseArray`. The proposal is to attach a tag, not change the
89	storage. Programs that ignore the tags still work.
90	
91	### Tier B: build once Tier A is in place
92	
93	| Concept             | Today                                       | Proposed surface           |
94	|---------------------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
95	| **Layer**           | a `ModelSpec` variant                       | a `Layer` role with `input_kind`, `output_kind`, and `params` |
96	| **Hidden layer**    | a non-final `Layer` in a `chain`           | a `Layer` with `is_hidden=true` (set automatically by `chain`) |
97	| **Activation layer**| `Activation(ActKind)` in `ModelSpec`        | first-class `ActivationLayer` role with no params              |
98	| **Optimizer**       | `momentum_sgd` / `adam` built-ins           | an `Optimizer` role carrying state across calls               |
99	| **Schedule**        | `cosine_schedule` / `linear_warmup` scalars | a `Schedule` role with a `step(t)` interface                  |
100	| **Dataset**         | tuples of `DenseArray` produced by `moons`  | a `Dataset` role with `inputs`, `labels`, `n_classes`, etc.   |
101	| **Trace**           | the `Trace` JSON                            | a typed `Trace` value queryable from MLPL                     |
102	
103	These are mostly *upgrades* to things that already exist; the
104	goal is to attach explicit role metadata so the language can
105	surface it.
106	
107	### Tier C: research-grade, plan but defer
108	
109	These overlap with the paper-driven backlog
110	(`docs/paper-driven-development.txt`) and deserve their own
111	sagas before they get types.
112	
113	- **Memory module** (paper #3 Engram, paper #13 MSA): tag rows
114	  in an external memory table with their freshness, source, and
115	  retrieval count.
116	- **Skill** (paper #10): a typed `Skill` value bundling code +
117	  prompt + tests + permissions.
118	- **Tool** (paper #4): a typed `Tool` value with a schema and an
119	  invocation channel.
120	- **Episode / rollout / reward** (paper #4, #7, #8): typed RL
121	  primitives with structured trajectories.
122	- **Plan / executor** (paper #8 PEARL): typed plan trees that
123	  can be inspected before execution.
124	- **Voices / debate / critic / judge** (paper #19): typed
125	  multi-perspective reasoning roles.
126	
127	Each of these is ambitious enough that it should be designed as
128	its own subsystem first; the type tag is the *least* of the
129	work.
130	
131	## What `:describe` should print once tags exist
132	
133	Today (v0.7.0):
134	
135	    :describe W1
136	    W1 -- array
137	      shape: [2, 8] (trainable param)
138	      values: -0.1234 0.4567 ...
139	
140	Proposed (post-tags):
141	
142	    :describe W1
143	    W1 -- Weight (layer: encoder.linear_1)
144	      shape: [in=2, out=8]
145	      role:  trainable parameter
146	      init:  randn(seed=11) * 0.5
147	      grad:  not yet computed
148	      values: -0.1234 0.4567 ...
149	
150	`:describe` becomes the primary self-description surface for
151	typed values. Every tier-A tag carries enough metadata to
152	populate a few extra lines.
153	
154	## Where the tags live
155	
156	Two implementation paths, with different cost / benefit:
157	
158	### Path 1: side table on Environment
159	
160	Add `pub(crate) tags: HashMap<String, ValueTag>` to `Environment`.
161	A `set_tag(name, tag)` helper attaches a tag to a binding by
162	name. `:describe` reads the tag from the side table when
163	formatting.
164	
165	- Cheap: no change to `DenseArray`, no change to `Value`,
166	  no parser changes.
167	- Limited: tags only apply to *named bindings*. Anonymous
168	  intermediates lose their tag immediately.
169	- Good first step. Lets us answer "what is `W1`?" without
170	  invasive changes.
171	
172	### Path 2: typed wrapper around DenseArray
173	
174	Add a new `Value::Typed { array: DenseArray, tag: ValueTag }`
175	variant. Every op that produces a result either propagates the
176	tag or strips it. Built-ins gain tag-aware versions.
177	
178	- Expensive: every existing op needs to handle the new variant,
179	  every demo needs to check what gets stripped, the tag
180	  propagation rules are non-trivial (does `W1 + W2` produce a
181	  `Weight` or just an array?).
182	- Powerful: anonymous intermediates retain their identity. The
183	  loss `mean((apply(mdl, X) - Y) * (...))` could be tagged
184	  `Loss { kind: MSE }` automatically.
185	- Probably too much work for v0.7.x. Reserve for after Saga 11.5.
186	
187	**Recommendation:** start with Path 1 (side table). It is
188	additive, contained to `mlpl-eval`, and unblocks the `:describe`
189	improvements that motivate this proposal. Path 2 is the sequel.
190	
191	## Typing-assistance loop for users (and agents)
192	
193	The point of all this is to enable a *conversation* between the
194	user and the workspace:
195	
196	    mlpl> mdl = chain(linear(2, 8, 11), tanh_layer(), linear(8, 2, 12))
197	    mlpl> :describe mdl
198	    mdl -- chain(2 hidden layers, 1 output layer)
199	      input:  shape [n, 2]
200	      output: shape [n, 2]
201	      hidden activations: 1 (after linear_1, kind=tanh)
202	      params: 4 -- W1[2,8], b1[1,8], W2[8,2], b2[1,2]
203	    mlpl> :describe W1
204	    W1 -- Weight (layer: mdl.linear_0)
205	      shape: [in=2, out=8]
206	      role:  trainable parameter
207	      grad:  computed at last adam() call (step 47)
208	    mlpl> :hidden mdl 0     ; brand-new command
209	    [Activation tanh, layer mdl.linear_0]
210	    shape: [n, 8]
211	    last computed at step 47
212	
213	Every line of that session is unblocked by tagging. None of it
214	is unblocked by the language as it stands today.
215	
216	Agents benefit even more. A tagged value gives an LLM a
217	concrete schema to follow when constructing or repairing a
218	program: "I need a `Weight` of shape `[in, out]` to plug into
219	this `Linear` layer", instead of "I need an array, hopefully of
220	the right shape, hopefully not a bias, hopefully not a
221	gradient".
222	
223	## Open questions
224	
225	- **Tag propagation for anonymous values.** Tier-A side-table
226	  tags only attach to bindings. Do we want to add a
227	  "register on assign" rule so that `g = grad(loss, W1)` is
228	  automatically tagged `Gradient { wrt: W1 }`? Probably yes.
229	  How far does it go?
230	- **Subtyping.** Is a `Weight` also an `Array`? Yes -- ops that
231	  take an array should accept a tagged value transparently. The
232	  reverse is not true: a built-in that demands a `Weight` should
233	  refuse a plain array.
234	- **Mutation.** When `W1 = W1 - lr * grad(...)`, does the tag
235	  carry through the assignment? Yes if the rhs is "obviously" a
236	  weight update (Path 2 territory). With a side table, tags are
237	  per-name and survive reassignment by default.
238	- **User-defined tags.** Should users be able to define their
239	  own roles? `tag(x, "MyMemoryRow")`? Yes eventually, but
240	  probably not in the first step. Start with the curated Tier A
241	  vocabulary.
242	- **Interaction with named axes.** A `Weight` *and* labeled axes
243	  are complementary: the role says "this is a trainable weight
244	  matrix", the labels say "axis 0 is `in_features`, axis 1 is
245	  `out_features`". They compose without conflict.
246	- **Models as parameter trees.** `:describe mdl` should walk the
247	  ModelSpec and pretty-print each layer with its inferred input
248	  and output shapes. This is achievable today (even before
249	  tags) and could be a small follow-up.
250	
251	## Suggested first-step deliverable
252	
253	Something small and concrete to validate the approach before
254	committing to a full saga:
255	
256	> Add a `ValueTag` enum with the Tier-A variants, a
257	> `tags: HashMap<String, ValueTag>` side table on `Environment`,
258	> a `:describe` rendering that consumes the tag, and a
259	> `:tag <name> <kind>` REPL command for manually attaching a
260	> tag. Wire `linear()` and friends to auto-tag the params they
261	> create as `Weight` / `Bias`, and `grad()` to auto-tag its
262	> result as `Gradient { wrt }`. No new built-ins beyond `:tag`,
263	> no parser changes, no new `Value` variant. One commit, one
264	> step, fully reversible.
265	
266	If that lands cleanly and the `:describe` output proves useful
267	in practice, the next step is the same treatment for `Loss`,
268	`LearningRate`, `Labels`, and `Activation`. Then iterate.
269	
270	## Saga shaping
271	
272	This is at least one full saga's worth of work, possibly two:
273	
274	- **Saga 11.7 -- Typed ML concepts (Tier A):** `ValueTag`
275	  enum, side table, `:tag` / `:untag` REPL commands,
276	  auto-tagging from `linear()` / `chain()` / `grad()` / `adam()`
277	  / `cosine_schedule()`, expanded `:describe` output for tagged
278	  values, tutorial lesson "Typed ML Concepts", regression
279	  tests. ~6-8 steps.
280	- **Saga 11.8 -- Typed ML concepts (Tier B):** `Layer` /
281	  `Optimizer` / `Schedule` / `Dataset` roles, layer-aware
282	  `:describe mdl` walker that prints the model as a typed tree,
283	  contract checks at op boundaries (e.g. "loss expression for
284	  `adam` must be a `Loss`-tagged scalar"). ~6-8 steps.
285	
286	Tier C overlaps with the paper-driven backlog and should be
287	folded into the relevant feature sagas (memory in 18, skills
288	and tools in 18, etc.) rather than a single typing saga.
289	
290	## See also
291	
292	- `docs/typing.md` -- the *current* typing model (untyped
293	  homogeneous arrays).
294	- `docs/milestone-named-axes.md` -- Saga 11.5, which adds
295	  labeled axes (compatible and complementary).
296	- `docs/are-we-driven-yet.md` -- the audit that surfaced the
297	  gap between the agent-driven wishlist and what MLPL has today.
298	- `docs/paper-driven-development.txt` -- the paper backlog that
299	  most Tier C concepts will land alongside.
